Guanfacin (ATC code C02AC02) is a medication used in the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), specifically serving as a secondary treatment option for patients presenting with comorbidities [^src1]. Within the Danish national ADHD database, it is tracked as one of six core ADHD medications to monitor clinical practices and systemic treatment coverage [^src1].

In the context of national quality monitoring, Guanfacin is a key component of [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], which measures the coverage of pharmacological treatment among children and young people with ADHD in package pathways [^src1], [^src2]. As the database's scope expanded to include adult populations, Guanfacin was also integrated into the newly established [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]], which evaluates pharmacological treatment specifically for adults with ADHD [^src3]. Its inclusion alongside other primary medications—such as methylphenidate, dexamfetamine, modafinil, atomoxetine, and lisdexamfetamine—ensures that the national registry accurately captures the full spectrum of medical interventions across different demographics and regions [^src3].
